extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners working on humor generation and LLM alignment
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, curating, and evaluating methods and datasets to make large language models produce high-quality humorous outputs, including persona-based data synthesis and preference-driven optimization. Focus is on methodology (Cognitive Synergy Framework), dataset creation, distillation to smaller models, and comparative evaluations against baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise and incongruity as essential to comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor generation requires surprise and incongruity, which inherently conflict with LLMs' standard training objective of predicting the most likely next word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the maximum-likelihood next-token objective discourages surprise; methods should explicitly account for or counteract this conflict to produce comedy (i.e., avoid only optimizing for most-likely continuations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretically grounded data creation (Cognitive Synergy Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a theoretically grounded methodology for generating high-quality humor data inspired by psychological theories of humor (the 'Cognitive Synergy Framework').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset creation should be informed by psychological theory rather than ad-hoc examples — theoretical grounding is a design principle guiding what constitutes high-quality humor data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixture-of-Thought (MoT) with cognitive personas
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy a Mixture-of-Thought approach using multiple cognitive personas (e.g., The Absurdist, The Cynic) to synthesize diverse comedic perspectives for a given prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instantiate distinct persona-based reasoning styles to generate varied comedic takes per prompt; explicitly enumerate and use multiple personas to increase diversity and cover different humor strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of comedic perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate and include diverse comedic perspectives for each prompt (achieved via multiple personas) to enrich the humor dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity across styles (absurdism, cynicism, etc.) is a criterion for dataset quality — avoid narrow single-style corpora that limit the model's comedic range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persona-based distillation to student models
rubrics_metrics.description: Use persona-based synthesized data to fine-tune (distill) a smaller 'student' model (example: a 7B-parameter model) so it can reproduce persona-driven humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distillation from persona-generated data is an explicit production strategy: curate persona outputs, then fine-tune a compact model rather than relying solely on large-scale instruction tuning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare alignment/optimization methods (DPO vs O-GRPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and compare optimization/alignment approaches such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and the proposed Offline Group Relative Policy Optimization (O-GRPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use head-to-head comparisons of alignment techniques as an evaluation axis; report whether novel methods (e.g., O-GRPO) improve over established approaches like DPO in the humor generation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference-driven evaluation / optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage preference-based signals (as in DPO) when optimizing models for humor, implying human or proxy preference judgments are a key evaluation/learning signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate preference data (human judgments or aggregated preferences) into training/evaluation pipelines to align model outputs with what humans find funnier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative performance against instruction-tuned and proprietary baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark models against larger instruction-tuned baselines and state-of-the-art proprietary models, aiming to outperform instruction-tuned baselines and be competitive with proprietary systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative/qualitative comparisons to both open and closed baselines are required to demonstrate practical effectiveness; report relative performance clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize cognitive-driven data curation over scale or alignment alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognitive-driven data curation (theory-informed dataset design and persona synthesis) is far more critical than alignment algorithms or model scale for effective humor generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize dataset quality and design choices as the primary lever for improving humor generation, rather than relying primarily on increasing model size or changing alignment algorithms.
